title: Hot and Sour Soup
subtitle: Thick Chinese soup with pork, mushrooms, and egg ribbons
excerpt: Hot and sour soup is a Chinese staple with a sharp vinegar tang and warm heat from white pepper. Pork, dried mushrooms, and egg ribbons sit in a thick, warming broth. It is a popular first course in Chinese restaurants and a favourite home recipe. It comes together in under 40 minutes.
sourceNotes: Hot and sour soup (suanla tang) is a staple of Chinese cooking, particularly in Sichuan and northern Chinese cuisines. The sour element comes from vinegar; the heat from white pepper or chilli. The soup is thick, warming, and packed with contrasting textures. It is a popular first course in Chinese restaurants worldwide.

content.text: The egg ribbon technique is what makes this soup distinctive. Adding the beaten egg in a slow, steady stream while stirring gently creates delicate wisps rather than hard lumps. Keep the heat low at that stage, and stir in one direction only. Soak the dried mushrooms for at least 20 minutes before you start cooking.

items.prepNote: soaked in hot water for 20 minutes, then drained and sliced
beaten -- drizzled in slowly at the end
mix with 4 tbsp cold water -- for thickening
white pepper works well here if available

content.text: Bring the stock to a simmer in a large saucepan. Add the ginger, mushrooms, and pork mince. Break up the mince with a spoon. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, vinegar, and chilli flakes. Taste and adjust the balance -- it should be clearly sour and mildly hot.
Stir in the cornflour-water mixture. Stir constantly until the soup thickens -- about 2 minutes.
Reduce heat to low. Pour the beaten eggs in slowly in a thin stream, stirring gently in one direction to create egg ribbons.
Season with salt and white or black pepper. Ladle into bowls and top with spring onion.

items.symptom: Egg has cooked into hard lumps rather than ribbons
items.cause: Heat too high or egg added too fast
items.fix: Reduce the heat to the lowest setting before adding the egg. Pour it from a height in a very thin stream while stirring gently in one circular direction. The result should be delicate wisps.

content.text: Hot and sour soup is a winter staple across northern China and Sichuan. The contrast between vinegar tang and white pepper heat is the soul of the dish. In restaurants it is often thickened more than home versions. The egg ribbons are one of the key textural elements.
